value.rationale: For quaternionic numerical ranges, failure of convexity is a central phenomenon; the four-dimensional volume added by convexification is a natural quantitative defect not captured by the previously known convexity criterion. For a canonical noncomplex 2-by-2 anticommuting pencil the result gives its exact dimensionless profile and sharp order-five onset at the convexity boundary. The profile is monotone and scales geometrically, giving a complete benchmark beyond a routine yes/no criterion; no general-purpose downstream theorem is asserted.
